ADVISORY_BODY: A calmer premarket after Tuesday's thud, but calmer is not the same as clear. Iran retaliated against U.S. bases overnight following Tuesday's American strikes on IRGC targets -- Brent is back up on the war premium. ADP printed the weakest private payroll gain since January (+38K), and the market's answer was to push Fed hike odds UP to 68.1%, not down -- a real divergence between cooling labor and a Fed (Warsh) still being priced as hawkish. VIX easing to 15.4 and real futures (Schwab /ESU26, /NQU26) both green say the tape wants to breathe. But the earnings reaction says otherwise: PANW and MDB both beat and got sold anyway, while only DELL's raise earned its pop. And crypto flatly isn't buying it -- BTC and ETH both red while equities are green. Doctrine: this is a provisional calm, not a confirmed regime shift. Half-risk discipline holds through Friday's NFP, the print that actually settles the hike question. The monkey moves when others freeze -- but freezing is still the correct read until the crosscurrents resolve one direction.
